source_text: Iam uero de solo suggestu et apparatu honoris retractandum. proprius habitus uniuscuiusque est tam ad usum quotidianum quam ad honorem et dignitatem. igitur purpura illa et aurum ceruicis ornamentum eodem more apud Aegyptios et Babylonios insignia erant dignitatis, quo more nunc praetextae uel trabeae uel palmatae et coronae aureae sacerdotum prouincialium, sed non eadem condicione. tantum enim honoris nomine conferebantur iis, qui familiaritatem regum merebantur. unde et purpurati regum uocabantur a purpura, sicut apud nos a toga candida candidati, sed non ut suggestus ille sacerdotiis quoque aut aliquibus idolorum officiis adstringeretur. nam si ita esset, utique tantae sanctitatis et constantiae uiri statim habitus inquinatos recusassent, statimque apparuisset Danielem idolis non deseruisse nec Belem nec draconem colere, quod multo postea apparuit. simplex igitur purpura illa nec iam dignitatis erat, sed ingenuitatis apud barbaros insigne. quemadmodum enim et Ioseph, qui seruus fuerat, et Daniel, qui per captivitatem statum uerterat, ciuitatem Babyloniam et Aegyptiam sunt consecuti per habitum barbaricae ingenuitatis, sic penes nos quoque fideles, si necesse fuerit, poterit et pueris praetexta concedi et puellis stola, nativitatis insignia, non potestatis, generis, non honoris, ordinis, non superstitionis. ceterum purpura uel cetera insignia dignitatum et potestatum insertae dignitati et potestatibus idololatriae ab initio dicata habent profanationis suae maculam, cum praeterea ipsis etiam idolis induantur praetextae et trabeae et laticlaui, fasces quoque et virgae praeferantur, et merito. nam daemonia magistratus sunt saeculi huius; unius collegii insignia fasces et purpuras gestant. quid ergo proficies, si suggestu quidem utaris, opera eius uero non administres? nemo in inmundis mundus uideri potest. tunicam si induas inquinatam per se, poterit forsitan illa non inquinari per te, sed tu per illam mundus esse non poteris. iam nunc qui de Ioseph et Daniel argumentaris, scito, non semper comparanda esse uetera et nova, rudia et polita, coepta et explicita, seruilia et liberalia. nam illi etiam condicione serui erant: tu uero nullius seruus, in quantum solius Christi, qui te etiam captiuitate saeculi liberauit, ex forma dominica agere debebis. ille dominus in humilitate et ignobilitate incessit domicilio incertus: nam filius, inquit, hominis non habet ubi caput collocet; uestitu incultus, neque enim dixisset, ecce qui teneris uestiuntur, in domibus regum sunt; uultu denique et aspectu inglorius, sicut et Esaias pronuntiauerat. si potestatis ius quoque nullum ne in suos quidem exercuit, quibus sordido ministerio functus est, si regem denique fieri conscius sui regni refugit, plenissime dedit formam suis derigendo omni fastigio et suggestu quam dignitatis quam potestatis. quis enim magis iis usus fuisset, quam dei filius? quales et quanti eum fasces producerent, qualis purpura de umeris eius floreret, quale aurum de capite radiaret, nisi gloriam saeculi alienam et sibi et suis iudicasset? igitur quam noluit, reiecit, quam reiecit, damnauit, quam damnauit, in pompa diaboli deputauit. non enim damnasset, nisi non sua: alterius autem esse non possunt, nisi diaboli, quae dei non sunt. tu si diaboli pompam eierasti, quicquid ex ea attigeris, id scias esse idololatrian. uel hoc te commonefaciat omnes huius saeculi potestates et dignitates non solum alienas, verum et inimicas dei esse, quod per illas aduersus dei seruos supplicia consulta sunt, per illas et poenae ad impios paratae ignorantur. sed et natiuitas et substantia tua molestae tibi sunt aduersus idololatrian. ad euitandum remedia deesse non possunt, cum et, si defuerint, supersit unicum illud, quo felicior factus non in terris magistratus, sed in caelis.
thought_title: The trappings of honor are idolatrous
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that even the outward dress and insignia of public office are contaminated by idolatry, using Joseph and Daniel as apparent counterexamples.
pass_a_gloss: Now truly about the mere seat and display of honor it must be reconsidered. The proper dress of each person is as much for daily use as for honor and dignity. Therefore that purple and the gold ornament of the neck among the Egyptians and Babylonians were insignia of dignity in the same manner, in which manner now the bordered togas or the trabeae or the palmatae and the golden crowns of the provincial priests, but not under the same condition. For only in the name of honor they were conferred on those, who were earning the familiarity of kings. Whence also the purple-clad of the kings were called from the purple, just as among us from the white toga the white-clad, but not so that that seat was bound also to priesthoods or to some offices of idols. For if it were so, certainly men of such great holiness and constancy would have immediately refused the defiled garments, and immediately it would have appeared that Daniel had not deserted to idols nor worshiped Bel nor the dragon, which appeared much later. Therefore that simple purple was no longer even of dignity, but was a mark of free birth among barbarians. For just as both Joseph, who had been a slave, and Daniel, who through captivity had changed his status, obtained the Babylonian and Egyptian citizenship through the dress of barbarian free birth, so among us also the faithful, if it is necessary, it will be possible both for boys a bordered toga to be granted and for girls a stola, marks of birth, not of power, of family, not of honor, of rank, not of superstition. But otherwise the purple or the other insignia of dignities and powers, inserted into dignity and into the powers of idolatry, dedicated from the beginning, have the stain of their profanation, since moreover also to the idols themselves are put on bordered togas and trabeae and laticlavi, also the fasces and rods are carried before them, and deservedly. For the demons are the magistrates of this age; of one college they carry the insignia, the fasces and the purples. What therefore will you profit, if you use indeed the seat, but do not administer its works? No one in unclean things can seem clean. If you put on a tunic defiled in itself, perhaps it will be able not to be defiled by you, but you will not be able to be clean through it. Now already you who argue from Joseph and Daniel, know that old and new things are not always to be compared, rough and polished, begun and completed, servile and free. For those men were also in the condition of slaves: but you are no one's slave, insofar as of Christ alone, who freed you also from the captivity of the age, you ought to act according to the Lord's pattern. That Lord walked in humility and obscurity, uncertain of dwelling: for the Son, he says, of man does not have where he may lay his head; uncultivated in clothing, for he would not have said, behold, those who are clothed in soft things are in the houses of kings; finally inglorious in face and appearance, just as also Isaiah had announced. If he exercised no right of power even over his own, for whom he performed a lowly service, if finally he fled being made king, conscious of his own kingdom, he most fully gave the pattern to his own by directing away all loftiness and display, both of dignity and of power. For who would have used these things more than the Son of God? What and how great fasces would escort him, what purple would bloom from his shoulders, what gold would radiate from his head, unless he had judged the glory of the age alien both to himself and to his own? Therefore what he did not want, he rejected; what he rejected, he condemned; what he condemned, he counted in the pomp of the devil. For he would not have condemned it, unless it were not his own: but they cannot be of another, unless of the devil, the things which are not of God. You, if you have renounced the pomp of the devil, whatever of it you will have touched, know that to be idolatry. Or let this remind you that all the powers and dignities of this age are not only alien, but also enemies of God, because through them punishments have been devised against the servants of God, through them also the penalties prepared for the impious are unknown. But both your birth and your substance are troublesome to you against idolatry. For avoiding it remedies cannot be lacking, since also, if they are lacking, that one thing remains, by which you are made more fortunate, not a magistrate on earth, but in heaven.

choices.english: the mere seat and display of honor
choices.why: Keeps the two nouns distinct: the physical elevated seat and the outward show, matching Tertullian's focus on external trappings.
rejected: the platform and pomp of office
the seat and splendor of honor

choices.why: Preserves the genitive 'of the kings' and the adjectival noun, showing the title derived from the garment.
Captures the legal status term 'ingenuitas' as free birth, not merely nobility, which is key to the Joseph and Daniel argument.
Uses the fixed glossary rendering for this key term from the baptismal renunciation.

choices.english: the demons are the magistrates of this age
choices.why: Keeps 'magistrates' for the political office term, showing the demonic claim to worldly authority.
rejected: demons are the rulers of this world
the demons hold office in this age

choices.english: you ought to act according to the Lord's pattern
choices.why: Renders 'forma' as pattern, emphasizing Christ's example as the model for conduct.
rejected: you must act by the Lord's form

pass_b_english: Now I must deal with the mere seat and display of honor. Each person has a distinctive dress, both for daily use and for honor and dignity. So that purple and the gold ornament for the neck were marks of dignity among the Egyptians and Babylonians in the same way that bordered togas, ceremonial robes, palm-embroidered robes, and golden crowns of provincial priests are now, but not under the same conditions. They were conferred only as a title of honor on those who deserved the friendship of kings. That is why they were called the purple-clad of the kings, from the purple, just as among us candidates are named from the white toga, but not so that this seat of office also bound them to priesthoods or any offices of idols. For if that had been so, men of such holiness and steadfastness would certainly have refused the polluted garments at once, and it would have appeared at once that Daniel did not serve idols or worship Bel or the dragon, which appeared much later. So that purple was simple, and no longer a mark of dignity but of free birth among the barbarians. For just as Joseph, who had been a slave, and Daniel, who had changed his status through captivity, obtained citizenship in Babylon and Egypt through the dress of barbarian free birth, so among us too, if necessary, the bordered toga can be allowed to boys and the robe to girls, marks of birth, not power; of family, not honor; of rank, not superstition. But the purple and the other marks of dignities and powers, attached to dignity and power, have been dedicated to idolatry from the beginning and carry the stain of their profanation, especially since bordered togas, ceremonial robes, and broad-striped tunics are also put on the idols themselves, and bundles of rods and staffs are carried before them. And rightly so. For the demons are the magistrates of this age; they carry the insignia of one college, the rods and the purple. What will you gain, then, if you use the seat of office but do not administer its works? No one can appear clean in unclean things. If you put on a tunic that is defiled in itself, perhaps it cannot be defiled by you, but you cannot be clean through it. Now, you who argue from Joseph and Daniel, know that old and new conditions, rough and polished, begun and completed, servile and free are not always to be compared. For they were also in the condition of slaves. But you are no one's slave, except Christ's alone, who freed you even from the captivity of the world, so you ought to act according to the Lord's pattern. That Lord walked in humility and obscurity, with no fixed home: for the Son of Man, he says, has nowhere to lay his head (Matthew 8:20). He was plain in dress, for he would not have said, Look, those who are clothed in soft garments are in the houses of kings. Finally, he was without glory in face and appearance, as Isaiah had also declared (Isaiah 53:2). If he exercised no right of power even over his own, for whom he performed humble service; if he fled from being made king, though he knew his own kingdom, he gave the fullest pattern to his own by directing them away from every eminence and seat, whether of dignity or of power. For who would have used these things more than the Son of God? What rods and how great would have escorted him, what purple would have bloomed from his shoulders, what gold would have shone from his head, if he had not judged the glory of the world alien to himself and his own? Therefore what he did not want, he rejected; what he rejected, he condemned; what he condemned, he counted in the pomp of the devil. For he would not have condemned it unless it were not his own. And things that are not God's cannot belong to anyone but the devil. If you have renounced the devil's pomp, know that whatever you touch from it is idolatry. Let this also remind you that all the powers and dignities of this age are not only alien to God but hostile to him, because through them punishments have been devised against God's servants, and through them the penalties prepared for the impious are ignored. But your birth and your property are troublesome to you in opposing idolatry. Remedies for avoiding it cannot be lacking, since even if they were lacking, that one remedy remains by which you are made fortunate, not as a magistrate on earth, but in heaven.

problems.quote: Now I must consider the mere seat and display of honor.
problems.source_quote: Iam uero de solo suggestu et apparatu honoris retractandum.
problems.why: Latin says the seat and display of honor must be rejected/withdrawn, not merely considered.
problems.fix: Now indeed the mere seat and display of honor must be rejected.
problems.ruling: retractandum means 'must be reconsidered/retracted,' not merely 'consider'; translator omits the force of the gerundive.

fixed: The Latin 'retractandum' means 'must be withdrawn/rejected', not 'must be considered', so the English misstates the source.

polish.changed: Clarified the contrast between Joseph and Daniel's slave status and the Christian's freedom in Christ, smoothed awkward phrases like 'uncultivated in dress' to 'plain in dress,' and made the flow of Tertullian's argument about honor, idolatry, and the Lord's example easier to follow aloud.

notes.why: Reference to apocryphal additions to Daniel (Bel and the Dragon); reader may not know this text.
notes.fix: Note: 'Bel and the Dragon = apocryphal story of Daniel refuting Babylonian idol worship.'

notes.why: 'Uncultivated' is odd for dress; likely means 'unadorned' or 'plain.'
notes.fix: Use 'unadorned in dress' or 'plain in dress.'

notes.why: Roman fasces (rods and axes) as symbols of magisterial authority; reader may not know this.
notes.fix: Note: 'bundles of rods = fasces, symbols of Roman magisterial authority.'

notes.quote: candidates are named from the white toga
notes.why: Roman political candidates wore white togas; word origin is obscure to modern reader.
notes.fix: Note: 'candidates = from Latin candidus, white; Roman candidates wore white togas.'
